research_question: Can a cross-venue price gap predict a profitable10second directional trade on just one venue? Can local large aggressive flow on a relatively thin book identify transient dislocations?

sources.title: Albers et al., Fragmentation, Price Formation, and Cross-Impact in Bitcoin Markets
sources.finding: Order-book/trade features predict subsecond Bitcoin returns across markets. Trading tests emphasize fee dependence. The paper separates out-of-sample testing; synthetic taker analysis omits some latency and impact effects. Historical centralized-Bitcoin results do not validate these2026LIT venues.

sources.title: Degryse et al., Aggressive Orders and the Resiliency of a Limit Order Market
sources.finding: Aggressive orders show partial subsequent reversal and persistent effects. Order-flow persistence and longer-term price changes mean large flow alone is not a reliable fade signal. Equity evidence, not crypto validation.

sources.title: Xu et al., Limit-order book resiliency after effective market orders
sources.finding: Chinese-stock data show different outcomes by order aggressiveness: recovery dominates after aggressive orders, continuation after less aggressive orders. Spread/depth recovery differs from tradable price recovery.

sources.title: Large, Measuring the resiliency of an electronic limit order book
sources.finding: In a historical LSE sample, replenishment after large trades was unreliable in most cases; when present it was fast. This supports measuring probability and delay separately; its numerical frequencies are not transferred to LIT.

sources.title: Lighter official account types
sources.finding: Read today: Standard0%maker/taker,300ms taker and cancel/modify latency. Model adds explicit100ms network delay. RH equivalent documentation not accessible today; RH profile remains an archived assumption checked against freshzero-fee metadata, not a new latency verification.

limitations: Cross-venue gap closure need not generate a favorable target return.
Illiquidity raises spread, exit risk and price impact as well as signal size.
Sparse or delayed public prints, omitted liquidations and trade batching limit causal labels.
Currentprototype heuristics do not establish venue leadership or classify informed flow.
